risk_signals.statement: CAR has risen steadily from 10.52% (FY2011) to a consistent 13-15% range from FY2018 onward, comfortably above the regulatory minimum throughout — capital position has strengthened even as profitability declined in recent years.

NPL ratio jumped sharply from 4.54% (FY2021) to 7.09% (FY2022), the highest point in the 13-year series, alongside provisioning for classified loans roughly doubling (BDT 5,131.60mn -> BDT 8,062.79mn). ROE fell from 14.70% to 8.87% the same year and continued declining to 7.92% in FY2023 — the weakest two-year profitability stretch since FY2014-2015.

ROE peaked at 17.55% (FY2017) and 16.55% (FY2018), the strongest two-year run in the series, coinciding with the lowest NPL ratio observed (3.79% in FY2017) — profitability and asset quality moved together in that period.

FY2024 and FY2025 both report loan-loss provisioning far below Bangladesh Bank's own requirement, and the gap widened: FY2024 required provision against loans/advances was BDT 38,167.71m against BDT 21,159.11m actually maintained (shortfall BDT 17,008.60m, i.e. 44.6% underprovisioned), rising to a required BDT 33,902.34m against only BDT 12,509.23m maintained in FY2025 (shortfall BDT 21,393.10m, 63.1% underprovisioned) as general/unclassified provisioning fell short for the first time alongside specific/classified provisioning. Both years' reported CRAR (13.07% FY2024, 12.52% FY2025) were computed without reflecting this shortfall, per the bank's own disclosure. Bangladesh Bank granted regulatory forbearance both years (Ref. DBI-4/110/2025-655 for FY2024; Ref. BSD-2/2203/2026-384 for FY2025) and no dividend was declared in either year. The FY2025 auditors' report elevates this to a formal Emphasis of Matter (opinion not modified) — a more severe treatment than FY2024, where it appeared only as a note-level disclosure. Provision coverage of classified loans (provision_classified / classified_loans) fell from 36.95% (FY2023) to 22.12% (FY2024) to 14.87% (FY2025), consistent in direction with the sector-wide FY2024-25 recognition event documented for other banks in this dataset (see _HANDOFF.md), though milder in coverage terms than ISLAMIBANK's 6.24%.

NPL ratio nearly tripled from 6.08% (FY2023) to 17.25% (FY2024) as classified loans rose from BDT 17,313.35m to BDT 51,761.70m, the sharpest single-year asset-quality deterioration in the 15-year series. NPL ratio then fell to 15.19% in FY2025, but this is largely a write-off effect rather than recovery: the bank executed its largest-ever single-year loan write-off (BDT 20,750.89m per the FY2025 Directors' Report) in the same year gross loans fell 4.7% (BDT 300,025.11m -> BDT 285,935.57m, yoy_growth_pct.gross_loans = -4.70) and provision held against classified loans fell from BDT 11,447.80m to BDT 6,457.13m. The underlying provisioning shortfall (see the fy2024_2025_provisioning_shortfall risk signal) actually worsened over the same period, so the improving headline NPL ratio should not be read as an asset-quality improvement on its own.

ROE collapsed from 7.92% (FY2023, itself already the weakest point in the series to that date) to 2.44% (FY2024) as profit after tax fell 68.9% (BDT 2,028.61m -> BDT 631.22m) on a near-doubling of total provision charges (BDT 2,681.80m -> BDT 4,352.17m) and a compressed net interest margin (2.00% -> 2.04%, essentially flat, while cost-to-income rose to 60.06%). ROE partially recovered to 4.59% in FY2025 as profit after tax grew 90.1% to BDT 1,199.87m, but this remains less than 59% of the FY2023 level and well below the FY2017-2018 peak of 17.55%/16.55% — and the FY2025 profit recovery coincides with sharply lower provisioning relative to what Bangladesh Bank calculated as required (see the fy2024_2025_provisioning_shortfall risk signal), so part of the reported earnings recovery is attributable to under-provisioning rather than underlying performance.

insights.historical_context: Mercantile Bank's long run (FY2011-2021) shows a generally sound trajectory: steadily strengthening CAR and no capital-adequacy breach at any point, alongside a first bout of credit-quality and profitability deterioration in FY2022-2023 (NPL to 7.09%, ROE down to 7.92%) that was mild by the standards of what followed. FY2024-2025 mark a much sharper break: NPL nearly tripled in FY2024 (6.08% -> 17.25%), profit after tax collapsed 68.9% the same year, and both years disclose a Bangladesh-Bank-forborne loan-loss provisioning shortfall (BDT 17,008.60m in FY2024, widening to BDT 21,393.10m in FY2025) that its own reported CRAR does not reflect — the FY2025 shortfall is significant enough that the independent auditors elevated it to a formal Emphasis of Matter. The FY2025 apparent NPL improvement (to 15.19%) is substantially a write-off effect (BDT 20,750.89m written off, the bank's largest ever in a single year) rather than a genuine recovery, since the underlying required-vs-maintained provisioning gap widened in the same year. This full pattern — rising capital ratio computed without regard to a growing, disclosed provisioning shortfall, paired with reported profit recovering even as the shortfall worsens — is the same shape (though smaller in absolute magnitude) as the sector-wide FY2024-25 recognition-vs-deferral divide documented for NBL, IFIC, and ISLAMIBANK elsewhere in this dataset (see _HANDOFF.md's 'What the data shows' section): reported profit and even reported CRAR are the least informative numbers in Mercantile Bank's FY2024-2025 story, and the required-provision/maintained-provision gap (now captured in quarterly/2024_Q4.json and quarterly/2025_Q4.json as required_provision_loans, provision_maintained_loans, and provision_shortfall_loans) is the metric that actually separates recognition from deferral here.
